results.title: DPT | Tiered Access Models
results.content: User Data Enclave ----------------- A user data enclave (UDE) is a secure computing environment that allows approved and authorized researchers to access restricted-use microdata for research purposes in a controlled environment at their own institution or organization.A user data enclave (UDE) is a secure computing environment that allows approved and authorized researchers to access restricted-use microdata for research purposes in a controlled environment at their own institution or organization. Virtual Data Enclaves --------------------- A virtual data enclave (VDE) is a secure computing environment that allows approved researchers to access restricted-use data for research purposes. Controlled Access Online Data Tools ----------------------------------- A Controlled Access Online Data Tool (CA-ODT) provides a computing environment that allows approved researchers to run tabulations on agency restricted-use data through an online website portal. Open Access Online Data Tools ----------------------------- An Open Access Online Data Tool (OA-ODT) provides a computing environment that allows any data user to run tabulations on agency restricted-use data through an online website portal. Providing increased access to federal data assets requires a shift from a binary system of access models (public-use data and restricted-use data) to a system of tiered access. Technological advances such as online data tools with built-in disclosure protections or virtual enclaves in a secure cloud setting, have enabled federal agencies to expand the number of access levels, or tiers. Federal agencies use multiple methods to make data available—each with its own set of access controls. * Access may be limited by restricting it to a federally-controlled data enclave or a controlled-virtual enclave. Agencies can use a variety of administrative, physical, technological, and statistical controls to reduce the risk of unauthorized access, use, or disclosure, while making data available to researchers. Some tiered access models may exclusively use controls along one of those dimensions (e.g., Public-use data, which relies exclusively on Safe Data). Other tiered access models may use some level of controls along all five dimensions (e.g., Physical Data Enclaves). Because each of these types of controls may impact the overall accessibility, cost, burden, or usefulness of the data in different ways, agencies seeking to improve data access can select the tiered-access models best suited to address their data users’ needs.

results.title: AutoSamp: Autoencoding k-Space Sampling via Variational Information Maximization for 3D MRI - PubMed
results.content: To address this challenge, we introduce a novel deep learning framework, AutoSamp, based on variational information maximization that enables joint optimization of sampling pattern and reconstruction of MRI scans. Experiments on public 3D acquired MRI datasets show improved reconstruction quality of the proposed AutoSamp method over the prevailing variable density and variable density Poisson disc sampling for both compressed sensing and deep learning reconstructions. We demonstrate that our data-driven sampling optimization method achieves 4.4dB, 2.0dB, 0.75dB, 0.7dB PSNR improvements over reconstruction with Poisson Disc masks for acceleration factors of R =5, 10, 15, 25, respectively. Prospectively accelerated acquisitions with 3D FSE sequences using our optimized sampling patterns exhibit improved image quality and sharpness. Furthermore, we analyze the characteristics of the learned sampling patterns with respect to changes in acceleration factor, measurement noise, underlying anatomy, and coil sensitivities. We show that all these factors contribute to the optimization result by affecting the sampling density, k-space coverage and point spread functions of the learned sampling patterns. Training and inference pipeline for AutoSamp: In the training phase (a), AutoSamp jointly learns a sampling pattern and a reconstruction network using a fully-sampled dataset. results.title: Low-rank modeling of local k-space neighborhoods (LORAKS) for constrained MRI
results.content: Based on this, we develop a novel and flexible framework for constrained image reconstruction that uses low-rank matrix modeling of local k-space neighborhoods (LORAKS). Finally, we assess the proposed optimization framework by providing empirical results in dynamic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction in the context of locally low-rank models with overlapping patches. These methods include partial Fourier, which leverages conjugate symmetry [13], [14]; parallel imaging, which utilizes coil-specific local signal modulations in multichannel receiver arrays [15], [16]; compressed sensing, which exploits compressibility of the data [17]; low-rank based methods which exploit the inherent redundancies in the data [18], [19]; and approaches that combine these priors [20]- [22]. Compressed sensing further accelerates MRI acquisition by non-uniform sampling and imposing appropriate constraints on the reconstruction models, such as image sparsity [14], [15], low rankness [16], [17], [18], [19], [20], or a combination of both [21], [22]. Deep Learning (DL) methods can reconstruct highly accelerated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans, but they rely on application-specific large training datasets and often generalize poorly to out-of-distribution data. Since each k-space segment is only acquiring part of the k-space data, the reconstruction of the phase compensated image from their partially parallel measurements is posed as a structured low-rank matrix optimization problem, assuming the coil sensitivities to be known. Methods A novel few-shot learning-based reconstruction framework is proposed, featuring a 3D variational network specifically designed for 3D TOF-MRA that is pre-trained on simulated complex-valued, multi-coil raw k-space datasets synthesized from diverse open-source magnitude images and fine-tuned using only two single-slab experimentally acquired datasets. Purpose: To propose a domain-conditioned and temporal-guided diffusion modeling method, termed dynamic Diffusion Modeling (dDiMo), for accelerated dynamic MRI reconstruction, enabling diffusion process to characterize spatiotemporal information for time-resolved multi-coil Cartesian and non-Cartesian data. In this work, we present a new method to reconstruct fMRI image series from sparsely sampled (k,t)-space data. We introduce a novel algorithm to reconstruct dynamic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data from under-sampled k-t space data. Representation using a low-rank model leads to new schemes for data acquisition and image reconstruction, enabling reconstruction from highly-undersampled datasets.

results.title: CMRxRecon: A publicly available k-space dataset and benchmark to advance deep learning for cardiac MRI | Scientific Data
results.content: CMRxRecon: A publicly available *k*-space dataset and benchmark to advance deep learning for cardiac MRI. # CMRxRecon: A publicly available *k*-space dataset and benchmark to advance deep learning for cardiac MRI. There has been growing interest in deep learning-based CMR imaging algorithms that can reconstruct high-quality images from highly under-sampled k-space data. To address this gap, we released a dataset that includes multi-contrast, multi-view, multi-slice and multi-coil CMR imaging data from 300 subjects. Imaging studies include cardiac cine and mapping sequences. Accelerated cine imaging effectively addresses these limitations by utilizing a reduced amount of k-space data, while still maintaining high reconstruction performance. Consequently, there has been a growing interest in accelerated CMR image reconstruction from highly under-sampled k-space data. To the best of our knowledge, previous available cardiac raw datasets mainly include OCMR18–open-access multi-coil k-space dataset for cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging. In this paper, we describe the first release of CMR raw k-space data that includes multi-contrast, multi-view and multi- channel cardiac imaging from 300 subjects. Figure 1 shows representative CMR images of cardiac cine and mapping released in the dataset. To further evaluate the feasibility of using the provided k-space data for undersampling image reconstruction tasks, we used the GRAPPA22. fastMRI: A publicly available raw k-space and DICOM dataset of knee images for accelerated MR image reconstruction using machine learning. 0)–open-access multi-coil k-space dataset for cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging*.
